meta.title: Signs in the Town Library
meta.textType: functional: signs and notices in a public building

paragraphs: On Saturday, June thirteenth, the Explorers visited the town library with Teacher Kim. At the entrance, there was a big notice. It said, "OPEN: Tuesday to Sunday, nine o'clock to six o'clock. CLOSED ON MONDAY." "If it is Monday, the library is closed," said Teacher Kim. "Today is Saturday, so we can go in." Each pair of children got a card. The card said, "Find five signs and write what they say." Lily worked with May, and Mia worked with Leo. The notice was their first sign.

Inside the library, May read the signs out loud, and Lily wrote them in her notebook. "QUIET, PLEASE." "NO FOOD OR DRINK." "TURN OFF YOUR PHONE." "RETURN BOOKS HERE." Leo looked at the sign about food and put his banana in his bag. "Why do libraries have so many signs?" asked Mia. "If people talk loudly, other people cannot read," said Teacher Kim. "If you eat in a library, the books can get dirty," she added.

Mia went to the information desk and asked a librarian, "Where are the animal books?" The librarian was a woman with glasses and a gray cardigan. "On Floor Two, next to the window," she said. "Are comic books available, too?" asked Leo. "Yes, they are," said the librarian. "If you want to borrow a book, ask at the desk." "You can keep it for two weeks." "You can also find our books online."

After that, the children went up to Floor Two. A sign with an arrow said, "CHILDREN'S CORNER, FLOOR TWO." The corner had low shelves with comics and magazines. Mia and May sat down and read about animals. Leo began to laugh at a comic, but he remembered the QUIET sign. He laughed very quietly.

Before the children left by the exit, Lily counted the signs in her notebook. She had all five signs. She also had an extra sign from the Children's Corner. That evening, she wrote them for the blog. Teacher Kim read the post first and smiled. "Signs are short, but they tell us a lot," said Lily.
